newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. jobs data trigger confusion for OLOs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobs data trigger confusion for OLOs.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds were in a state of confusion on Friday after the release of U.S. employment data for February, traders said.
"The figures are very good...and yet the reaction goes in the opposite direction," said Conrad Fieremans at Kredietbank.
At 1520 GMT, the benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.73 percent against 5.75 percent before the release. March futures, down 0.19 at 122.16 before the data, were up 0.08 at 122.43.
February non-farm payrolls grew by 339,000 jobs, exceeding the 230,000 average estimate economists had offered in a Reuters poll. But January and December growth were revised downward.
Economists said the U.S. employment picture remained healthy in February although the data did not seem likely to push the Federal Reserve closer to an official interest rate hike.
Fieremans said he expected OLOs and Bunds to show an upward technical correction before starting a slide in the weeks ahead.
"For the longer term the market seems pretty fragile," he said.
One trader said that chart-technically the June bund future contract could rise to 102.25 before possibly slithering to between 99 and 100.
OLOs and bond futures showed a change of tack later on with futures falling 0.20 to 122.15 -- near the intraday low of 122.12 -- and the benchmark 2007 yield rising to 5.75 percent.
The OLO/Bund yield spread, which had been hovering between five and eight basis points earlier today, was unchanged at six.
Fieremans said he expected it to stick to current levels, with a maximum of just over 10, in coming weeks.
